quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: To be easier to see on the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Weave back and forth in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help others see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you start riding.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road means:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must move to another lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same spots as on your motorcycle.
Take it right out on the highway.
Learn how it works in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn how it works in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe area before riding on the road.

questions.question: You have less grip for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, you have less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: A motorized bicycle or moped cannot go faster than:
questions.explanation: In California, a motorized bicycle or moped is defined as a vehicle with two or three wheels that cannot travel faster than 30 miles per hour on flat ground.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be used during daylight hours.
Be used without a driver license.
Be used by anyone with any type of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used by anyone with any type of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.explanation: Put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a light on the speedometer that shows when you are in neutral.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may have poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal plates and utility hole covers.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear right away.
Weave side to side until you cross the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven bridge gratings, stay relaxed and go straight across at a steady speed. Weaving side to side is more dangerous than the weaving caused by the gratings.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, how should it fit?

options.text: Loose, so it flaps in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Your jacket should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind. It should be tight enough for protection but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent attention than cars. You must check for problems before riding, especially before riding at high speeds on the highway.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you to see better with its lights.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being hit from behind.
Reduce your speed and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and stay farther behind other vehicles. You cannot see as well in the dark, so you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the lead rider. This way, experienced riders can watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: When another motorcycle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding to the side near the passing driver increases the chance of a collision. Riding to the far side may cause them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury?
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injury. Speed does not matter — a helmet is always the best protection.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a position that lets you control the motorcycle with your arms. Do not sit in a way that requires your arms to hold up your body weight.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle during normal riding?

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on with the high beam whenever it is safe and legal. This helps others see your motorcycle day and night.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should you do if another vehicle arrives at the same time as you?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Why is it difficult to stop while turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: The motorcycle has less grip available for braking while leaning.
Riders focus on the turn and not on braking.
The brakes do not work during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle has less grip available for braking while leaning.
questions.explanation: While turning, the motorcycle uses traction to lean into the turn. This means less traction is available for stopping. You can brake while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: What can help reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury while riding. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face in a crash.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, how should motorcyclists ride?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Change to single-file when turning, in curves, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: What should you be aware of while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Only what is in front of you.
What is both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: What is both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: You must watch what is ahead of you, but do not ignore what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: If you need to brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve as separate actions. Never brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may only cause them to tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What can help reduce the chance of a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your actions, keep safe space around you, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: Where can a motorcyclist NOT place a toll road transponder?
questions.explanation: Transponders can be placed in your pocket, in a net on the gas tank, on a license plate device, in a storage compartment, or on the windshield. The toll reader must be able to detect it. Under the seat is not an approved location.
